correctness.rationale: For a rank-one real design, the entire sketch-and-solve error row equals the sketched residual cross term divided by sketched leverage. For iid Gaussian columns this has law Z^T R/sqrt(X), where X is chi-square with ell degrees and Z is independent N(0,I) in the (n-1)-dimensional orthogonal complement. For Haar orthonormal columns the leverage is Beta(ell/2,(n-ell)/2); rotational invariance gives independent spherical direction and error sqrt(Y/X) S^T R with Y chi-square(n-ell). Independent Beta((n-ell)/2,(ell-1)/2) times the squared radius of Z has chi-square(n-ell) law, establishing a *joint multi-output* error-vector coupling. The positive beta factor strictly below one gives strict all-threshold stochastic order for nonzero R; beta moments and a dominated small-chi-square CDF expansion prove the moments and exact tails. Verified all formula boundaries n>ell>=2, rank one, R=0 exception, arbitrary d and p, exact arithmetic; 845 seeded/exact standalone checks passed. No finite Monte Carlo outcome is used to justify an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: An expected-error advantage does not certify the probability that a numerical least-squares sketch exceeds a specified tolerance. The full independent-beta coupling supplies an all-quantile guarantee for arbitrary numbers of right-hand sides, and exact heavy-tail coefficients even where moments diverge. The n=10, ell=4 rank-one-residual benchmark separates mean-error attenuation 2/3 from catastrophic-tail attenuation 16/33, providing a concrete design-reliability distinction beyond routine rewriting of a known expectation. Its exact rank-one domain is natural as the smallest regression problem with nonzero residual.
